output:
I'll start by reading the docs and the existing code.

The output was truncated. I'll read the spec in pieces.

That call was malformed. I'll write the fixes with file edits instead.

Naming, quoting and grouping all behave as specified. Now I'll write the status file.

The `export` command is finished and follows `docs/export.md`. All 28 unit tests pass with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. Beyond the tests, I ran it by hand against `/app/store` with several locales and options. I did not check every rule in the spec.

What I fixed or completed under `/app/tally`:
- **`--where`:** `evaluate` in `export/expr.py` was missing. Any comparison, `~`, `in` or `not in` on a null is false. `is null`, `is not null` and `not` work as specified.
- **Locale numbers:** grouping now uses `group_sizes` and `min_grouping`. Before, it always grouped in threes. `en-IN` gives `12,34,567.50`. `--no-grouping`, the locale's `minus` and the "all-zero is never negative" rule are covered.
- **Date patterns:** I wrote the missing date and datetime pattern formatting. It handles the longest-token match, the 12-hour clock and `A`.
- **Canonical dates:** years below 1000 are now zero-padded.
- **CSV text:** the old code used Python's `csv` module, which quotes differently from section 8. I replaced it with hand-written quoting. Records end in CRLF, and the null token is never quoted. A value equal to the null token is quoted, and so is one that begins or ends with a space or tab.
- **`--sort`:** an explicit `nulls-first` or `nulls-last` was being flipped by `:desc`. It now holds in both directions. Without a placement, nulls still sort as larger than every value.
- **`--max-rows` file names:** the suffix is now taken from the last `.`, and a leading-dot name has no suffix. The number is three digits or wider when needed. `a.tar.gz` becomes `a.tar-001.gz`.
- **Store reading (outside the `export` code):** `tally/store/store.py` split part files with `splitlines()`. That breaks records containing U+2028 and similar characters, so I switched it to splitting on `\n`.

I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; cat docs/export.md docs/overview.md docs/conventions.md; find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | grep -v __pycache__ | head -100; git status | head

cd /app; for f in tally/cli.py tally/textio.py tally/errors.py tally/commands/__init__.py tally/commands/export.py tally/export/*.py tally/store/*.py tally/fmt/locales.py tally/fmt/numbers.py tally/fmt/dates.py tally/sorting.py tally/where.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done
cd /app; cat tests/test_export.py tests/support.py; cat locales/de-CH.json locales/en-IN.json; cat docs/commands.md | tail -60
cd /app; for f in tally/export/*.py tally/store/schema.py tally/store/store.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done
cd /app; sed -n 150,400p tally/export/expr.py; echo ======; cat tally/export/order.py

cd /app; python - <<'E'
import json,glob
for f in sorted(glob.glob('locales/*.json')):
    d=json.load(open(f,encoding='utf-8')); print({k:v for k,v in d.items() if k!='name'}, d['name'])
E
grep -rlP '\x{2028}|\x{2029}|\x{85}|\x0b|\x0c' store tests/fixtures | head; cat store/*/schema.json | head -120

cd /app; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -15; python -m tally export orders --locale en-IN --columns id,total,placed --sort status:desc:nulls-first,id:desc --max-rows 100 | head -8; python -m tally export customers --locale fr-FR --columns credit_limit,signup,vip,name --where "vip is null or name ~ 'a'" --null NA | head -5; python -m tally export events --locale en-IN --columns at,amount,value --sort amount:nulls-first | head -5

cd /app; python -m tally export customers --locale en-IN --columns credit_limit --sort credit_limit:desc | head -4; python -m tally export customers --locale sv-SE --columns credit_limit --sort credit_limit | head -3; cd /tmp && rm -rf o && python -m tally --store /app/store export products --out o/.x.tar.gz --max-rows 1 --columns id && ls o | head -3; python -m tally --store /app/store export products --out o/v.d/p --max-rows 1 --columns id; ls o/v.d | head -3; python -m tally --store /app/store export products --where "id = null"; echo $?

cd /app; rm -rf /tmp/o; python -m tally export customers --locale en-IN --columns credit_limit --where 'credit_limit > 99999' --delimiter tab | head -4 | od -c | head; python -m tally export products --out /tmp/o/.x.tar.gz --max-rows 1 --columns id && ls -a /tmp/o | head -3; python -m tally export products --out /tmp/o/v.d/p --max-rows 1 --columns id; ls /tmp/o/v.d | head -3; python -m tally export products --where "id = null"; echo $?; ls /app

cd /app; f=$(python -m tally export products --no-header --columns '' 2>&1 | head -1); python -m tally export products | head -2; python -m tally export products --out /tmp/o/.x.tar.gz --max-rows 1 --columns sku && ls -a /tmp/o | head -3; python -m tally export products --out /tmp/o/v.d/p --max-rows 1 --columns sku; ls /tmp/o/v.d | head -3

cd /app; rm -rf /tmp/o; cat > STATUS.json <<'E'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Finished the export command: implemented --where evaluation, locale grouping (group_sizes/min_grouping) and date/datetime patterns, CSV quoting per section 8 with CRLF, null-placement in --sort, and --max-rows file naming. Also made store line splitting robust to U+2028 and similar characters; the unit tests pass."}
E
